The actual invitation is to bring one small nonelectric household item, inspect its condition and decide whether a repair is possible. Make a precise ink typographic composition whose alignment and joined reading space come from adjusting the loose pivot of a tabletop mirror. The participant's decision, not a huge object image, organizes the poster. Use fresh composition, not a giant central photo surrounded by caption islands and not a generic notice table with a decorative tool.

Visual idea: a small, precise functional ink LINE DRAWING of a folding tabletop mirror occupies a restrained area alongside the upper headline. The whole small household object must be identifiable: rounded rectangular mirror frame, folding wooden support, a metal pivot screw and a narrow loose joint gap. Draw one slim flathead screwdriver visibly engaged in that pivot screw. Use consistent clean line widths and sparse contours; no photographic textures, shading clouds, exploded diagram, decorative callout, leader arrows, isolated tools, hands or people. The screwdriver shaft and the two connected mirror parts establish a real alignment direction which the headline and the continuous reading measure follow. Keep the drawing small enough that all long conditions have generous uninterrupted reading width. The drawing must show an actual engaged tool/object relation rather than just floating near the title. Do not invent a completed repair.

Design typography and space together: build the substantial headline from two complete phrase lines, "고쳐 쓰는" then "토요일", as strongly weighted Korean ink type with precise optical alignment and a deliberate short offset that resolves into one shared spine. Preserve every word and ordinary glyph shape; do not fracture, distort or collage characters. The two title lines and the connected joint drawing form one intentional assembly. The recruitment phrase is clearly subordinate and adjacent. Place the application deadline and its entire URL immediately adjacent to the headline as a confident first-reading pair, in compatible normal-width type. It can wrap at the space after the colon, but the complete URL must remain an intact, easy-to-read line. Do not horizontally squeeze it or switch to a compressed display texture. Use one controlled vermilion accent only for the application line and the tiny real joint detail; deep near-black ink for all other text on a plain warm-white ground. Crisp stable ink; no distressed texture, tape effect, fake handwriting, grain, gradients, glow or fake paper simulation.

Below that first invitation/application assembly, make all remaining information one continuous broad reading architecture, sharing a common left alignment and consistent normal body widths and baselines. It should feel like parts brought into proper alignment, not blocks wandering around an image silhouette. Dates, session/entry times, location and age/capacity form a coherent adjacent logistics group. The bringing sentence and excluded-items sentence form the next coherent group. Tools/parts cost and condition-check/non-guarantee follow in a useful comfortable line rhythm. Participation fee, photography consent and contact complete the same continuous reading space. Use the order of these meaningful groups to clarify the participant's decision, with spacing and weight rather than any new headings or marks. Keep equal semantic levels at equal body scale; give the long required sentences real line width and generous line spacing. A long sentence may wrap only at ordinary Korean word spaces into at most two well-balanced lines, never into tiny narrow fragments. No body copy may be relegated to microtype or a detached bottom strip. All fourteen exact values must be readily readable at an actual 720px-wide square view. Title and application should remain the first recognizable reading at 320px, while body is fully legible at 720px.

Only the following fourteen text values may appear, every value exactly once. Preserve Korean spelling, spaces, numerals, punctuation, en dash, middle dots, colon, comma, URL hyphen/dot/slash and English lowercase. Permitted line breaks between complete words within one value do not change the copy. No paraphrase, translation, omissions, duplicate text, extra labels, headings, slogans, numbers, logos, watermarks, badges, icons, decoration pretending to be information or invented promises. The scaffold instructions and quoted delimiters must not be printed.
